text:
You need a way to use Jamf to set a custom URL homepage for the Chrome app on iPad devices and deploy it across your fleet.

I’m Tobias Reyne, and I’d be glad to help you set this up cleanly and quickly. I have 7 years of experience building web and full stack solutions with JavaScript, TypeScript, React, Next.js, Node.js, PostgreSQL, REST API, Tailwind CSS, Stripe, HTML, and CSS, and I’m comfortable working on practical deployment tasks like this where the goal is a reliable configuration rather than a big build.

A project that’s relevant here was a clipboard sync browser extension for Clipboardly, a productivity software client. I built a Chrome extension in TypeScript with the Chrome Extensions API plus an Express API and MongoDB backend to sync saved snippets across devices. That product reached 9k weekly active users and maintained a 4.7 store rating. While that project was broader than a homepage configuration, it did require careful Chrome extension work, browser behavior awareness, and making sure the end result was stable across devices.

For your Jamf + Chrome on iPad setup, I’d focus on the fastest path to a working homepage URL that can be deployed to your iPad fleet with minimal friction. I can help review the Jamf configuration, confirm the right Chrome app settings for iPad, and make sure the homepage URL is structured so it opens correctly for your users. Since you’re looking for only 1–2 hours of help, I’d keep the scope tight and practical: identify the right setting, validate the configuration, and leave you with a clear deployment path.

If you already have the homepage URL ready, I can likely move very quickly. If not, I can still help you determine the best format and implementation approach before you push it through Jamf.

Would you like me to help you set this up with a homepage URL you already have, or do you need assistance deciding what URL and Jamf setting should be used?
